subject: Genetics
title: What Dominant Really Means
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Dominant Really Means.

hook.text: Dominant doesn't mean better or more common. It just means one copy is enough to show the trait. That's all.

buildup.text: If you carry one brown-eye allele and one blue-eye allele, your eyes are brown. Brown is dominant over blue.

discovery.text: A dominant allele masks the recessive one. You need two recessive copies (homozygous) to show the recessive trait.

twist.text: Huntington's disease is dominant. One copy kills you. Polydactyly (extra fingers) is dominant.

climax.text: Dominance is about molecular mechanism, not survival advantage. A gene either makes enough protein or it doesn't.

quiz.question: What does 'dominant' mean in genetics?
options: One copy is enough to show the trait
